A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Superman, with matching methods, equations, and principal experiments. Their complete text and rendered figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison; the shorter v2 contains identifiable removals rather than extraction gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original Human3.6M and 3DPW experiments, component ablations, computational measurements, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results, tokenizer and multi-task ablations, computational measurements, and appendix visualizations.

M1.justification: The dual-stream Vision-Guided Motion Tokenizer, hybrid quantization, VSA, optional MAFT, Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone, objectives, and task procedures remain unchanged. Omitted implementation details and experimental variants do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Human3.6M, unseen-dataset evaluation on 3DPW, and the three principal tasks remain. However, v2 removes the video-only and skeleton-plus-video motion prediction/in-betweening scenarios reported in v1 Table 6. The shortened action breakdown does not establish that those actions were excluded from evaluation.

E2.justification: The external comparator sets in Tables 2–4 remain unchanged. Deleting v1 Table 7 nevertheless removes quantitative comparisons against the no-VSA/no-MAFT baseline and the MAFT-only variant. MotionGPT3's venue update does not introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: The reported scaling design contracts from 3B/7B/8B, including Qwen3-VL-8B, to 3B/7B. The tokenizer sweep also loses its MAFT-enabled evaluation condition. Retained benchmark splits, preprocessing, metrics, and input protocols are unchanged; omitted training settings are documentation losses rather than evidence of changed training.

E4.justification: v2 removes the visual-input generation and VSA/MAFT component ablations, narrows tokenizer and scaling analyses, and deletes appendix analyses of cross-frame attention, cross-joint alignment, and features before/after MAFT. These substantially reduce component and mechanism validation. VSA sampling and semantic-sphere analyses remain, with the latter renumbered from Figure S13 to S7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Approximation symbols added to computational figures do not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 4 and retained Table 3 values are unchanged. However, v2 removes seven action categories' scores, visual-input generation results including skeleton-plus-video MP/MIB errors of 23.30/25.63, component-ablation results, the MAFT-enabled tokenizer column, 8B scaling results, and several qualitative attention findings. This substantially reduces reported evidence without establishing improved performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, including hybrid-codebook selection, tokenizer loss, and autoregressive objectives in Equations 1–6, is retained. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs that change between versions.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims: unified perception and generation, a visually grounded motion vocabulary, competitive or state-of-the-art performance, and scalability. Reduced supporting evidence does not itself change these claims.

C2.justification: v2 removes substantive explanations attributing generation gains to visual contextual cues and component gains to VSA–MAFT synergy. It also removes interpretations of MAFT attention as demonstrating temporal tracking, joint-level semantic correspondence, and background suppression. This substantially narrows the mechanistic discussion, although VSA error correction and codebook-semantic interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 omits the HRNet-w48 specification, encoder layer counts and downsampling factor, stream dimensions, LoRA targets and rank, and MAFT head count and hidden dimension. Appendix A also drops the three-epoch MLLM training duration. These details are not restored elsewhere. A new code-repository URL provides an access pointer, but its contents are not established by the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: The first related-work paragraph shifts from single-task pose estimation to traditional multi-task perception models. v2 adds MTVCrafter and Point-in-Context reference entries and removes Integral Human Pose Regression. The overall positioning of Superman remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses implementation and results prose, rewrites one related-work paragraph, updates affiliations, adds acknowledgements, and shortens the appendix subsection structure. Most wording and the principal narrative order remain intact; the larger reductions primarily remove scientific content rather than extensively rewrite it.

P2.justification: v2 removes the pose-estimation pipeline diagram and two ablation tables, truncates the action and tokenizer tables, and redraws and relocates the scaling plot. Appendix Figures S7–S12 and S14–S15 disappear, while the semantic spheres move from S13 to S7. Figure 1 is also revised. These materially change the visual presentation beyond pagination.

improvement.justification: v2 retains the core method and headline benchmark evidence, streamlines presentation, and adds a code pointer. However, removing direct visual-grounding and VSA/MAFT ablations alongside key replication settings weakens evidential completeness and reproducibility. Substantial benchmark and appendix validation remains, limiting the overall decline.
